nahhas-irab:1-3.t: Abū Jaʿfar said: this [غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ ... سَيَغْلِبُونَ] is the reading of most people. It is reported from Abū ʿAmr and Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī that they read (الَم غَلبَتِ الرُّومُ) [i.e. with the active غَلَبَت] and read (سَتُغْلَبُونَ) [Translator's note: so in the source; the intended form is the passive سَيُغْلَبُونَ]. Abū Ḥātim reported that ʿIṣma narrated from Hārūn that this is the reading of the people of Syria; Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal says that this ʿIṣma is weak, while Abū Ḥātim narrates a great deal from him. The ḥadīth indicates that the reading is غُلِبَتِ with ḍamma on the ghayn. In this report there was a proof of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, because Persia had defeated the Romans, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, announced that the Romans would defeat Persia within a few years, and that the believers would rejoice at that because the Romans were People of the Book. This was part of the knowledge of the unseen that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, announced before it had happened. He commanded Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, to wager with them on that and to raise the wager; then wagering was forbidden and abrogated by the prohibition of gambling. (وَهُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ غَلَبِهِمْ): al-Farrāʾ claimed that the original was من بعد غلبتهم and the tāʾ was dropped, as it was dropped in His saying (وَأَقامَ الصَّلاةَ) [al-Nūr: 37]. This is an error that is not hidden from many grammarians, because «أقام الصلاة» [i.e. إقامة] is a maṣdar (verbal noun) from which something was dropped because its verb is weak, and the tāʾ was made a compensation for what was dropped; whereas «غلب» is not weak and nothing was dropped from it. Al-Aṣmaʿī reported: طرد طردا, حلب حلبا and غلب غلبا — so what dropping is there in this? And may one say about أكل أكلا and the like that something was dropped from it?

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: (ثُمَّ كانَ عاقِبَةَ الَّذِينَ) [Translator's note: the comment treats this as the nominative reading عاقِبَةُ, although the source prints the accusative vowel]: the noun of كان; [the verb] is masculine because its femininity is not real. (السُّواى) is the khabar of كان. Whoever reads (عاقِبَةَ) in the accusative makes «السّوأى» the noun of كان. It is reported from al-Aʿmash that he read ثمّ كان عاقبة الذين أساؤا السّوءُ, with السوء in the nominative. (أَنْ كَذَّبُوا) is in the position of the accusative, and the meaning is "because they denied".

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read (يُبلَس) with fatḥa on the lām. What is known in the language is أبلس الرجل, when a man falls silent, his argument cut off, with no hope of having an argument; close to it is "he was bewildered", as the rajaz poet said:
336-
قال: نعم أعرفه وأبلسا
(He said: "Yes, I know it", and fell silent in despair.)
Some grammarians claimed that «إبليس» is derived from this, and that he "despaired (ablasa)", that is, his argument was cut off. Had it been as he said, it would have to be fully declinable, yet in the Qurʾān it is a diptote. Some of them argued that it is a noun that was felt heavy because no one else was named by it.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: (وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُمْ مِنْ شُرَكائِهِمْ شُفَعاءُ): it is said: by "their partners" He means what they worshipped besides Allah, Mighty and Majestic. (وَكانُوا بِشُرَكائِهِمْ كافِرِينَ): they said: they are not gods.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
(فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): I heard Abū Isḥāq say: the meaning of «أمّا» is "leave what we were on and take up something else". Likewise Sībawayh said that its meaning is مهما يكن من شيء ("whatever may be the case"), that is: whatever may be the case, take up something other than what we were on. (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; (فَهُمْ) is a second mubtadaʾ, what follows is its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of «الذين». Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: (فِي رَوْضَةٍ): in a garden; and الرياض are gardens. Abū ʿUbayda said: الروضة is what is in low ground; if it is elevated it is a تُرعة. Someone else said: a meadow is at its finest when it is in an elevated, rugged place, as al-Aʿshā said: [basīṭ] 337-
ما روضة من رياض الحزن معشبة
(No grassy meadow of the rugged uplands [is more fragrant than she].)
Except that it is not called a روضة unless there is vegetation in it; if there is no vegetation in it and it is elevated, it is a تُرعة; and other things have been said about الترعة. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «يحبرون» means "they are honoured". Al-Kisāʾī reported حبرته, that is, I honoured him and favoured him. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: it is derived from their saying على أسنانه حبرة, that is, a trace [on his teeth]; so يحبرون means the trace of bliss shows on them; and الحبر is derived from this.

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: The exegetes hold that this concerns the prayers. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: its true meaning in my view is "glorify Allah in the prayers", because glorification (tasbīḥ) takes place in the prayer. It is reported from ʿIkrima that he read فسبحان الله حينا تمسون وحينا تصبحون; it is accusative as an adverbial (mafʿūl fīhi), and the meaning is: "a time in which you enter the evening and a time in which you enter the morning", so that something from the qualifying clause refers back to حين; its like in the Qurʾān is (يَوْماً لا تَجْزِي نَفْسٌ عَنْ نَفْسٍ شَيْئاً) [al-Baqara: 48]. Abū Jaʿfar said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: the prepositions are not dropped; rather only the hāʾ is implied in it.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: (وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ): the accusative is also possible, as a maṣdar.

nahhas-irab:20-21.t: (وَمِنْ آياتِهِ أَنْ خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ تُرابٍ): (أَنْ) is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; likewise (أَنْ خَلَقَ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَزْواجاً لِتَسْكُنُوا إِلَيْها). (وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَكُمْ مَوَدَّةً وَرَحْمَةً): it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: المودّة ("affection") is a man's love for his wife, and الرحمة ("mercy") is his mercy towards her lest harm befall her.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made clear His signs that point to Him: the creation of the heavens and the earth, the variety of the tongue in the mouth, the variety of languages, and the variety of colours and forms despite the great number of people, so that you hardly see anyone without being able to distinguish him from another. This is among the strongest proofs of the Disposer and Creator, because one who made something other than this would not have this differentiation in it.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: (وَمِنْ آياتِهِ أَنْ تَقُومَ السَّماءُ وَالْأَرْضُ بِأَمْرِهِ): that is, they stand without pillars by His power; He called it a "command" figuratively, as one says: "this is a great matter (amr)". On the meaning of (يَسْمَعُونَ) [Translator's note: this word belongs to the preceding verse, al-Rūm: 23] there are two views: "they accept", like his saying سمع الله لمن حمده ("Allah hears (accepts) whoever praises Him"); and the other is that among them were some who, if the Qurʾān was recited while they were present, stopped their ears so as not to hear. When He, Mighty and Majestic, had made clear the proof of Himself, He said: (ثُمَّ إِذا دَعاكُمْ دَعْوَةً مِنَ الْأَرْضِ إِذا أَنْتُمْ تَخْرُجُونَ), that is, the One who did these things is able to raise you. The readers agree on fatḥa on the tāʾ here in «تخرجون» [i.e. تَخرُجون], but they differ over the one in «al-Aʿrāf»: the people of Medina read (وَمِنْها تُخْرَجُونَ) [al-Aʿrāf: 25], and the people of Iraq read it with fatḥa, and Abū ʿUbayd inclines to that. The two meanings are close, except that the people of Medina distinguished between them because of the sequence of the discourse: the sequence of the discourse in the one in «al-Aʿrāf» fits better with ḍamma, since death is not their own act, and so likewise the bringing out; while fatḥa in Sūrat al-Rūm fits better with the sequence of the discourse, that is: when He calls you, you come out, that is, you obey; so the act is more appropriately attributed to them.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: Abū al-Haytham reported from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: «Every qunūt in the Qurʾān is obedience.» Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning is: all who are in the heavens and the earth are obedient to Him with the obedience of their submission to whatever He wills of health and sickness, wealth and poverty; this is not the obedience for which they are rewarded.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: (وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ): we have discussed it. (وَلَهُ الْمَثَلُ الْأَعْلى): that is, whatever He, Mighty and Majestic, wills comes to be. Al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, said: المثل is the attribute.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: (شُرَكاءَ) is in the position of the nominative, and (مِنْ) is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis. (فَأَنْتُمْ فِيهِ سَواءٌ): mubtadaʾ and khabar; سواء here is not the one that is an adverb. (تَخافُونَهُمْ كَخِيفَتِكُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ): accusative through the verb [i.e. the maṣdar]; the kāf and mīm are in the position of the genitive, and they are also in the position of the nominative by interpretation, as you say عجبت من ضربكم عمرا ("I wondered at your striking ʿAmr"). من ضربكم عمرو is also possible, because the maṣdar is annexed to the agent and to the object. You say: عجبت من وقع أنيابه بعضها على بعض ("I wondered at the striking of his canines one upon another"), and if you wish you put [بعضها] in the nominative, because أنيابه is in the position of the nominative by interpretation; but the nominative with an overt noun is ugly according to the Kufans. If you said عجبت من وقعها بعضها على بعض, the nominative would be good according to all. (كَذلِكَ): the kāf is in the position of the accusative, and the implied form is: "We set out the signs in detail, a detailing like that".

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: (بَلِ اتَّبَعَ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أَهْواءَهُمْ): plural of هوى, because its origin is faʿal.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: (فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ): that is, set your direction towards the religion. (حَنِيفاً): as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «حنيفا» means a Muslim who performs the pilgrimage. He said: and (فِطْرَتَ اللَّهِ) is the religion of Allah. Abū Isḥāq said: «فطرة الله» is accusative in the sense of "follow the natural disposition (fiṭra) of Allah"; he said: because the meaning of (فَأَقِمْ وَجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ) is "follow the religion and follow the fiṭra of Allah". Muḥammad ibn Jarīr [al-Ṭabarī] said: «فطرة» is a maṣdar from the meaning of فأقم وجهك, because its meaning is: Allah created people upon that with a creating (fiṭra). We have discussed "the fiṭra of Allah" at greater length than this in «al-Maʿānī», and the ḥadīth «Every child is born upon the fiṭra», and the views of the jurists on it. It is said: its meaning is that he is born with the constitution that you know. And it is said: the meaning of "the fiṭra of Allah upon which He created people" is: follow the religion of Allah for which He created people. The fiṭra was called a religion because people are created for it; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: (وَما خَلَقْتُ الْجِنَّ وَالْإِنْسَ إِلَّا لِيَعْبُدُونِ) [al-Dhāriyāt: 56]. And someone argued from His saying, Mighty and Majestic: (وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَها) [al-Isrāʾ: 7] [i.e. that "for it" may mean "against it"].

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: (مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ) is accusative as a ḥāl. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: because the meaning of «فأقم وجهك» is "so set your faces". This is the view of Abū Isḥāq, and he argued from His saying, Mighty and Majestic: (يا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ) [al-Ṭalāq: 1]. Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is "so set your face, you and those with you, turning [to Him]". Abū al-ʿAbbās rejected the view of whoever said the implied form is "they do not know, turning [to Him]", because the meaning of منيبين is "returning", so how could it be "they do not know, returning"? Moreover, after it comes (وَاتَّقُوهُ); its meaning is only: "so set your faces and fear Him (وَلا تَكُونُوا مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ)".

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: (مِنَ الَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوا دِينَهُمْ): ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, Abū Hurayra and Abū Umāma, may Allah have mercy on them both, interpreted it as referring to the people of the qibla [the Muslims]. Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas said: those who divided their religion are the People of the Book. وفارقوا دينهم [the variant reading] means they abandoned their religion which they ought to follow, namely tawḥīd. (وَكانُوا شِيَعاً): that is, factions. (كُلُّ حِزْبٍ بِما لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ): it is said: they rejoice because they have not discerned the truth, though they are obliged to discern it. It is said: this was before the proofs became manifest. A third view is that one who disobeys Allah, Mighty and Majestic, may rejoice in his disobedience, and likewise Satan, highway robbers and others; and Allah knows best. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the complete stop may be at «ولا تكونوا من المشركين», the meaning [continuing] «من الذين فارقوا دينهم» (وَكانُوا شِيَعاً) as a new sentence (resumptive), and that it may also be connected to what precedes it. Abū Jaʿfar said: if it is connected to what precedes it, then according to the Basrans it is a badal with the repetition of the preposition, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: (لِلَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا لِمَنْ آمَنَ مِنْهُمْ) [al-Aʿrāf: 75]; and had it been without the preposition, it would be permissible.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: (دَعَوْا رَبَّهُمْ مُنِيبِينَ إِلَيْهِ): as a ḥāl. From Ibn ʿAbbās: that is, turning to Him with all their hearts.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: (لِيَكْفُرُوا بِما آتَيْناهُمْ): the lām of purpose (lām kay). It is also said: it is the lām of command carrying the sense of threat, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: (فَمَنْ شاءَ فَلْيُؤْمِنْ وَمَنْ شاءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ) [al-Kahf: 29], and as you say: "speak to so-and-so, until we see what befalls you from me". Likewise (فَتَمَتَّعُوا); and what indicates that is (فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ).

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: (أَمْ أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطاناً): a question carrying the sense of making them stop and acknowledge (tawqīf). Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: «سلطانا», that is, a book. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the Arabs make السلطان feminine, saying قضت به عليك السلطان ("the authority [fem.] decreed it against you"). As for the Basrans, the masculine is more eloquent in their view, and the Qurʾān came with it; the feminine is permissible in their view because it means "proof (ḥujja)". Our saying سلطان means "one who has authority", that is, one who has the proof. However, Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said otherwise, in what ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān reported to us from him; he said: سلطان is the plural of سليط, as you say رغيف and رغفان; so its masculine is according to the sense of "all" and its feminine according to the sense of "group".

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: (وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِما قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِذا هُمْ يَقْنَطُونَ): the implied form according to Sībawayh is قنطوا ("they despaired"); that is why it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: (فَآتِ ذَا الْقُرْبى حَقَّهُ): Mujāhid and Qatāda interpreted it as a man's relative, and made maintaining kinship ties an obligation from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so much so that Mujāhid said: charity is not accepted from anyone while his kin are in need. And it is said: ذو القربى is kinship with the Prophet ﷺ, and his due is made clear in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: (وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّما غَنِمْتُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي الْقُرْبى) [al-Anfāl: 41]. «وابن السبيل» ("the wayfarer") is the guest, so He made hospitality an obligation. (فَأُولئِكَ) is a mubtadaʾ, (هُمُ) a second mubtadaʾ, (الْمُضْعِفُونَ) the khabar of the second, and the clause is the khabar of the first. There are two views on the meaning of المضعفين: one is that good deeds are multiplied for them; the other is that good and bliss have been multiplied for them, that is, they are possessors of multiples, as one says فلان مقو, that is, he has strong companions [or mounts]; and one says فلان رديء مردئ, that is, he is bad in himself and his companions are bad.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
(فِي بِضْعِ سِنِينَ): the hāʾ was dropped from بضع to distinguish masculine from feminine. The nūn of سنين was given fatḥa because it is a sound plural. Some Arabs say في بضعِ سنينٍ [with the nūn inflected], as they say من غسلينٍ. If that is permissible, [it is because] سنة was given a plural with wāw and nūn and yāʾ and nūn because something was dropped from it, and this plural was made a compensation. The sīn was given kasra, whereas it had fatḥa in سنة, because the kasra was made an indication that it is a plural formed otherwise than it should be. This is the view of the Basrans. Al-Farrāʾ would be obliged to give it ḍamma, except that he says: the ḍamma is an indication of the wāw; and a wāw was dropped from سنة according to one of the two views, yet no one we know gives it ḍamma. (لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَمِنْ بَعْدُ): one also says من قبلٍ ومن بعدٍ. Al-Kisāʾī reported from some of the Banū Asad: (لِلَّهِ الْأَمْرُ مِنْ قَبْلٍ وَمِنْ بَعْدُ) [Translator's note: the source prints the standard vowelling; the description that follows fixes the forms], the first genitive with tanwīn and the second with ḍamma without tanwīn. Al-Farrāʾ reported «من قبلِ ومن بعدِ», both genitive without tanwīn. Al-Farrāʾ has, in this section of his book on the Qurʾān, many things in which the error is plain. Among them: he claimed that «من قبلِ ومن بعدِ» is permissible, as the poet said: [majzūʾ al-kāmil] 332-
إلّا علالة أو بداهة ... سابح نهد الجزاره
(Except for the second run or the first burst of a swift steed, stout of limb.)
And as he said: [munsariḥ] 333-
يا من رأى عارضا أكفكفه ... بين ذراعي وجبهة الأسد
(O who has seen a cloud I keep watching, between the Forearms and the Forehead of the Lion [i.e. the lunar mansions].)
The error in this is plain, because the Qurʾān does not have لله الأمر من قبلِ ومن بعدِ ذلك, so that it would be like his saying «بين ذراعي وجبهة الأسد». Do you not see that you say أخذته بنصف وربع الدرهم ("I bought it for a half and a quarter of the dirham"), but it is not permissible to say أخذته بنصف وربع [with neither annexed]; and you say قطع الله يد ورجل زيد ("may Allah cut off the hand and foot of Zayd"), but it is not permissible to say يد ورجل [alone]. Moreover, this too is not common in the speech of the Arabs, and the Book of Allah is only interpreted according to what is common and eloquent; it is not permissible to make an analogy on it with what does not resemble it. If you said اشتريت دار وغلام عمرو ("I bought the house and the slave of ʿAmr"), it would not be permissible according to anyone we know. Among them [his errors]: he claimed that من قبلِ ومن بعدِ is permissible while you intend the annexation. This undoes the whole chapter, because the ḍamma was in it only because of the absence of the annexation while intending it; so if you put it in the genitive while intending it, the speech contradicts itself. «من قبلٍ ومن بعدٍ» is only permissible on the basis that they are both indefinite. Abū Isḥāq said: the meaning is "from something earlier and from something later". Among them: he likened من قبل ومن بعد to their saying من علُ, and recited: [rajaz] 334-
إن تأت من تحت أجئها من عل
(If you come from below, I will come at her from above.)
But من قبل ومن بعد are not of the type of من عل. Sībawayh said: they did not make vowelless, among nouns, what resembles the fully declinable noun, nor what has been put in a position like that of the non-declinable. What resembles [the declinable] is «من علُ», which they gave a vowel because they say من علٍ; as for the declinable noun that has been treated like the non-declinable, it is their saying ابدأ بهذا أولُ ("begin with this first") and يا حكمُ ("O Ḥakam"). Do you not see that Sībawayh, by his precision [Translator's note: the source has «لحذفه», likely for لحذقه, "his skill"], distinguished between «من عل» and «أول»? Then al-Farrāʾ came and combined them, and recited what we have mentioned, and recited: [ṭawīl] 335-
فو الله ما أدري وإنّي لأوجل ... على أيّنا تعدو المنيّة أوّل
(By Allah, I do not know — and I am fearful — upon which of us death will first descend.)
So he mixed them all in the chapter and brought both of them under «قبل وبعد», though one of them differs from قبل وبعد.
As for the discussion of قبل and بعد according to the doctrine of Sībawayh and of the Basrans: their way is not to be inflected, because the annexed-to noun and the annexation had been dropped from them, so they became definite without a means of definiteness, and their full declinability departed. They could not be left without a vowel because they had been declinable, so ḍamma was chosen for them, because genitive and accusative can reach them by right of inflection, so they were given a vowel other than those two, and they were given ḍamma. However, Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: since they are both "limits" (ghāya), they were given what is the furthest (ghāya) of the vowels. (وَيَوْمَئِذٍ يَفْرَحُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ): there are two views on its meaning. One is that they rejoice at the Romans' victory over Persia, because the Romans are People of the Book and so nearer to the Muslims than the idolaters. The other view, which is more fitting, is that their joy is only at the fulfilment of the promise of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, since there was in it a proof of the prophethood, because He, Mighty and Majestic, announced what would happen within a few years, and it happened.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t:
(ظَهَرَ الْفَسادُ فِي الْبَرِّ وَالْبَحْرِ بِما كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِي النَّاسِ): there are two views on its meaning. One is: drought appeared on land, that is, in the deserts, and he read it: "and in the sea", that is, in the cities of the sea, like (وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ) [Yūsuf: 82]; that is: scarcity of rain and high prices appeared because of the sins that people's hands have earned, so that He might make them taste the punishment of some of what they did; then [this] was omitted. The other view is that the meaning of (ظَهَرَ الْفَسادُ) is: sins appeared — highway robbery and oppression — and this is corruption in the true sense; the first is figurative. But on the second answer there is an ellipsis and abridgement in the discourse, indicated by what follows it; the meaning would be: sins appeared on land and sea, so Allah withheld the rain from them and made their prices high, in order to make them taste the punishment of some of what they did (لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ). Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind reported from ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās: «لعلهم يرجعون» means "so that they may repent".
As for His saying, Mighty and Majestic: (وَما آتَيْتُمْ مِنْ رِباً لِيَرْبُوَا فِي أَمْوالِ) [al-Rūm: 39], we have mentioned the view of the scholars on it: that it is a man giving another man a gift, intending a return for it and not intending reward [from Allah]; that is permitted, except that he is not rewarded for it, because he did not intend by it the reward of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. However, al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: the Prophet ﷺ in particular was forbidden that, by His saying, Mighty and Majestic: (لا تَمْنُنْ تَسْتَكْثِرُ) [al-Muddaththir: 6]. And it is said: the meaning of "whatever you give of ribā" is the ribā that is not lawful; the holder of this view said: the meaning of "it does not increase with Allah" is that it is not adjudged to the one who takes it, because it is not his, but belongs to the one from whom it was taken. The dual of الربا is ربوان; so says Sībawayh, and nothing else is permissible according to his followers. I heard Abū Isḥāq say, mentioning the view of the Kufans: it is not enough for them, in saying ربيان, that they err in orthography by writing الربا with yāʾ; they even err in the dual — and he considered this serious. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: (لِيَرْبُوَا فِي أَمْوالِ النَّاسِ), and this makes it clearer that it is a wāw-final root, and that the view is as Abū Isḥāq said.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: (مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لا مَرَدَّ لَهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ): that is, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will not turn it away from them, and if He does not turn it away, no one is able to repel it. According to grammarians other than Sībawayh «لا مردٌّ له» [with nominative and tanwīn] is permissible, but according to Sībawayh that is far-fetched unless there is a conjunction in the discourse. (يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصَّدَّعُونَ): the original is يتصدّعون; the tāʾ was assimilated into the ṣād because of their closeness. One says تصدّع القوم when people disperse; and from it الصّداع ("headache") is derived, because it splits apart the parts of the head.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: (كانَ حَقًّا عَلَيْنا): the khabar of كان. (نَصْرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ): its noun. Had it been outside the Qurʾān, it would have been permissible to put حقّ in the nominative and نصر in the accusative, because حقّا, though indefinite, is followed by علينا; and it would have been permissible to put both in the nominative, by implying [a pronoun of the matter] in كان with the khabar being the clause. In the ḥadīth: «Whoever defends the honour of his companion, Allah will turn the fire of Hell away from him»; then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited (وَكانَ حَقًّا عَلَيْنا نَصْرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ).

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: (وَيَجْعَلُهُ كِسَفاً): plural of كسفة, which is a piece. In the reading of al-Ḥasan, Abū Jaʿfar and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Aʿraj it is كِسْفا with sukūn on the sīn; it too is a plural of كسفة, as one says سدرة and سدر. On this reading the pronoun after it refers back to it, that is: "and you see the rain coming out from between the pieces", because every plural that differs from its singular only by the hāʾ may well be treated as masculine. Whoever reads كِسَفا, the pronoun refers in his view to the clouds [Translator's note: the source has «الحساب», read as السحاب]. In the reading of al-Ḍaḥḥāk: فترى الودق يخرج من خلله ("from its gap"); and خلال may be the plural of خلل.

nahhas-irab:49-50.t:
(وَإِنْ كانُوا مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمُبْلِسِينَ) (49) (فَانْظُرْ إِلى آثارِ رَحْمَتِ اللَّهِ كَيْفَ يُحْيِ الْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِها إِنَّ ذلِكَ لَمُحْيِ الْمَوْتى وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ) (50)
(وَإِنْ كانُوا مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمُبْلِسِينَ): we have discussed it. Abū Isḥāq held that it is for emphasis, and said that Quṭrub's view that the implied form is "before the sending down" is wrong, because the rain is inseparable from the sending down. He recited: [ṭawīl] 338-
مشين كما اهتزّت رماح تسفّهت ... أغاليها مرّ الرّياح النّواسم
(They walked, swaying as spears sway whose tops are tossed by the passing of gentle winds.)
He made المرّ ("passing") feminine [in تسفّهت] because the winds are inseparable from it, and because the meaning is "the winds tossed their tops"; so likewise the meaning of «من قبل أن ينزل عليهم المطر» is "before the rain". One says آثر and إثر. (كَيْفَ يُحْيِ الْأَرْضَ): assimilation is not permissible in it, lest two vowelless letters come together.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: (وَلَئِنْ أَرْسَلْنا رِيحاً فَرَأَوْهُ مُصْفَرًّا): it is said: the implied form is "they saw the crops turning yellow"; it is said: "they saw the clouds"; and it is said: "they saw the wind", الريح being made masculine because what is meant is the one sent of it. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: there is nothing to prevent making masculine any noun of unreal femininity, such as أعجبني الدار ("the house pleased me") and the like. (لَظَلُّوا): al-Khalīl, may Allah have mercy on him, said: its meaning is ليظلّنّ ("they would surely remain"). Abū Isḥāq said: this is permissible because there is the sense of requital (mujāzāh) in the discourse.

nahhas-irab:52-53.t: (فَإِنَّكَ لا تُسْمِعُ الْمَوْتى وَلا تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ الدُّعاءَ): they were put in the position of the dead and the deaf because they do not benefit from what they hear. (وَما أَنْتَ بِهادِي الْعُمْيِ عَنْ ضَلالَتِهِمْ): al-Farrāʾ said: من ضلالتهم is also possible, in the sense of "you cannot hold them back from their misguidance"; and عن in the sense of "you cannot turn them away from their misguidance".

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: (اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ ضَعْفٍ): ʿAṭiyya reported from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah have mercy on him, who said: I recited to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ «من ضَعف», and he said to me: (مِنْ ضَعْفٍ) [i.e. ضُعف]. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read (مِنْ ضَعْفٍ) [i.e. ضُعُف], and the Kufans read (مِنْ ضَعْفٍ), which is the maṣdar [Translator's note: the source prints all the forms with the same vowelling; the vowels given here follow the known readings: Ḥamza and Shuʿba ضَعف, the rest ضُعف]. The grammarians among them allowed من ضَعَف, and likewise every word in which a guttural letter is second or third. Abū Isḥāq said: its interpretation is: Allah is He who created you from the sperm-drop, your state with which is weakness; then after weakness He made youth.

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: (وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السَّاعَةُ يُقْسِمُ الْمُجْرِمُونَ ما لَبِثُوا غَيْرَ ساعَةٍ): there is no rejection of the punishment of the grave in this, since it has been authenticated from the Prophet ﷺ through more than one chain that he sought refuge from it and commanded that refuge be sought from it. Among that is what ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd narrated: he ﷺ heard Umm Ḥabība saying: "O Allah, let me enjoy my husband the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, my father Abū Sufyān and my brother Muʿāwiya." The Prophet ﷺ said to her: «You have asked Allah about appointed lifespans and allotted provisions; rather ask Him to protect you from the punishment of Hell or the punishment of the grave», among well-known ḥadīths. On the meaning of (ما لَبِثُوا غَيْرَ ساعَةٍ) there are two views. The first is that it means there must be a stillness before the Day of Resurrection, and the annihilation decreed upon creation overtakes both those shown mercy and those punished; on this basis they said "we remained only an hour", because they did not know [Translator's note: the source has «يعملوا», read as يعلموا] its extent. The other view is that they mean in this world, because of its passing away and coming to an end, even though they swore about the unseen and about what they did not know. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: (كَذلِكَ كانُوا يُؤْفَكُونَ), that is, thus they used to lie in this world. A group of the theologians (ahl al-naẓar) claimed that there cannot be lying at the Resurrection because of the state they are in, but the Qurʾān indicates otherwise. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: (كَذلِكَ كانُوا يُؤْفَكُونَ), and He, exalted be His praise, said: (يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعاً فَيَحْلِفُونَ لَهُ كَما يَحْلِفُونَ لَكُمْ وَيَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ عَلى شَيْءٍ أَلا إِنَّهُمْ هُمُ الْكاذِبُونَ) [al-Mujādila: 18].

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: The believers answered them, saying: (لَقَدْ لَبِثْتُمْ فِي كِتابِ اللَّهِ إِلى يَوْمِ الْبَعْثِ). Abū Isḥāq said: that is, in the Preserved Tablet. Yaʿqūb reported from one of the readers «إلى يوم البَعَث» [Translator's note: the variant vowelling is not shown in the source; by the following remark it is البَعَث with fatḥa on the ʿayn]; this is a word containing a guttural letter.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: (فَيَوْمَئِذٍ لا يَنْفَعُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مَعْذِرَتُهُمْ): when the believers answered them, they asked to return to this world and offered excuses, but they were not excused. (وَلا هُمْ يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ): nor is their state that of one who is asked to make amends and so returns.

nahhas-irab:58-58.t:
(وَلَقَدْ ضَرَبْنا لِلنَّاسِ فِي هذَا الْقُرْآنِ مِنْ كُلِّ مَثَلٍ وَلَئِنْ جِئْتَهُمْ بِآيَةٍ لَيَقُولَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ أَنْتُمْ إِلاَّ مُبْطِلُونَ) (58)
(وَلَقَدْ ضَرَبْنا لِلنَّاسِ فِي هذَا الْقُرْآنِ مِنْ كُلِّ مَثَلٍ): [parables] that guide them to what they need.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: An emphatic maṣdar (mafʿūl muṭlaq, absolute object). Abū Isḥāq said: (وَعْدُ اللَّهِ) in the nominative is also possible, in the sense of "that is the promise of Allah". (وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لا يَعْلَمُونَ): they are the disbelievers, and they are the majority.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: (وَلا يَسْتَخِفَّنَّكَ) is in the position of the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibition; it was emphasised with the heavy nūn and so made indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, as two things are made indeclinable when one is joined to the other. (الَّذِينَ لا يُوقِنُونَ) is in the position of the nominative; some Arabs say الذّون in the nominative position.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: (يَعْلَمُونَ ظاهِراً مِنَ الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا): then He made clear what they are ignorant of by His saying: (وَهُمْ عَنِ الْآخِرَةِ هُمْ غافِلُونَ). The first «هم» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), the second is a second mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the first; there is a sense of emphasis in the discourse. The second «هم» may also be a badal (substitute) for the first, as you say رأيته إياه ("I saw him, him"); there is also a sense of emphasis in the discourse.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: (وَإِنَّ كَثِيراً مِنَ النَّاسِ بِلِقاءِ رَبِّهِمْ لَكافِرُونَ): the lām is for emphasis, and the implied form is لكافرون بلقاء ربّهم, by fronting and postponing. On this basis you say: إنّ زيدا في الدار لجالس ("Zayd is in the house, sitting indeed"); and if you said إنّ زيدا لفي الدار لجالس, it would be permissible. But if you said إنّ زيدا جالس لفي الدار, it would not be permissible, because the lām is brought only to emphasise the noun and khabar of إنّ, so once you have brought them [without it], it is not permissible to bring it. Likewise if you said إنّ زيدا لجالس لفي الدار, it would not be permissible.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: (وَأَثارُوا الْأَرْضَ): because the people of Mecca were not people of tillage [Translator's note: the source has «حرب» ("war"), likely for حرث ("tillage"); translated according to the context].
